issue.close_reason: Pinned all three external tool versions (yq v4.44.1, kubectl v1.29.6, cloudflared 2024.8.1) at the top of bootstrap.sh and updated their installation sections to use these explicit versions instead of resolving 'latest' at runtime. This ensures reproducible bootstraps and avoids the :latest anti-pattern.
issue.description:
ex44/bootstrap.sh installs three tools by resolving "latest" at run time
instead of pinning a version, the same anti-pattern this workspace's own
CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids for container images ("Never use :latest image
tags - always pin to a specific digest or version tag"):

- yq: `curl ... api.github.com/repos/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest | jq -r
  '.tag_name'` (falls back to hardcoded v4.40.5 if that call fails - which
  will itself silently go stale as the true latest moves further away).
  ex44/bootstrap.sh ~line 480.
- kubectl: `curl -s https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt` - whatever is
  "stable" today. ex44/bootstrap.sh ~line 547.
- cloudflared: `.../cloudflared/releases/latest/download/...` ~line 842.

Effect: bootstrapping a new host next month can silently install different,
untested tool versions than what was bootstrapped and verified today, and
the yq GitHub API call is subject to anonymous rate limiting (60 req/hr)
which could fail intermittently with no useful fallback other than an old
hardcoded version.

Fix: pin explicit versions as variables near the top of the script (e.g.
YQ_VERSION, KUBECTL_VERSION, CLOUDFLARED_VERSION), matching the semantic
versioning discipline the script already applies to itself (VERSION/
START_SH_VERSION). Bump deliberately when needed, not automatically.
issue.title: Pin external tool versions instead of resolving latest at bootstrap time (yq, kubectl, cloudflared)

issue.description:
ex44/README.md's Security Features section states the SSH hardening posture
as "No root login" and implies TCP forwarding is disabled, matching the
script's original hardened defaults. The current ex44/bootstrap.sh SSH
config (sshd_config.d/hardening.conf, Step 7, ~line 683) has since drifted
from that stated posture without an explanation in the repo:

- `PermitRootLogin prohibit-password` (was `PermitRootLogin no`)
- `AllowTcpForwarding yes` (was `AllowTcpForwarding no`)
- `AllowUsers root $ALLOW_USERS_LIST` (root added to the allow-list, was just
  $ALLOW_USERS_LIST)

Each change may well be intentional (e.g. TCP forwarding needed for some
workflow like kubectl-proxy tunneling, root access needed for the Hetzner
rescue-network emergency-access path already documented in the Recovery
section) - but right now there's no comment or ADR explaining why, and
README.md's "Security Features" prose still describes the pre-drift,
stricter posture, so a reader comparing the two would reasonably conclude
this is unintentional regression rather than a deliberate tradeoff.

Action: investigate git history/commit messages for why these three settings
changed, then either (a) tighten them back to match the documented posture,
or (b) update README.md's Security Features section to accurately describe
the current, looser posture and add a one-line comment in the sshd config
heredoc explaining the tradeoff. Don't leave the doc and the config
disagreeing silently.

File: ex44/bootstrap.sh ~line 683-722; ex44/README.md Security Features
section.
issue.title: Resolve and document SSH hardening tradeoff: AllowTcpForwarding yes + PermitRootLogin prohibit-password

issue.description:
ex44/README.md documents a "Verification Commands" section listing 8 manual
commands an operator is expected to run one at a time after bootstrapping
(ufw status, tailscale status, sshd -T | grep ..., docker run hello-world,
fail2ban-client status sshd, auditctl -l, sysctl -a | grep ..., ncdu /).
There's no automated way to confirm a host actually ended up in the
hardened/working state bootstrap.sh intended - only bootstrap.sh --version
exists as a flag today.

Add a `bootstrap.sh --verify` (or `--check`) subcommand that runs each of
those checks programmatically and prints a PASS/FAIL summary (e.g. "UFW:
PASS (deny incoming, tailscale0 allowed)", "SSH hardening: FAIL
(PasswordAuthentication yes)"). Useful both right after a fresh bootstrap and
periodically afterward (e.g. after an unattended-upgrades run that might
have reset something), and turns the README's manual checklist into
something a NEEDLE worker or cron job can run unattended and alert on.

File: ex44/bootstrap.sh (new top-level flag alongside the existing
--version/-v handling ~line 20-24); README.md's Verification Commands
section (~line 145-165) is the checklist to encode.
issue.title: Add 'bootstrap.sh --verify' to automate the README's manual Verification Commands checklist

Implemented optional OpenBao secret sourcing for B2 credentials in ex44/bootstrap.sh

Fixed typo in OpenBao URL (traefil-rs-manager → traefik-rs-manager:8200) and added

OpenBao fetch. The script now:

1. Checks if OPENBAO_TOKEN environment variable is set
2. Verifies Tailscale is installed and active (required for OpenBao over tailnet)

without manual entry each run, while keeping manual prompts as fallback. Updated README
to document the feature and fixed pre-commit hook path (ex44/ → hosts/ex44/).

issue.description:
ex44/bootstrap.sh currently requires a human to type the B2 Application Key
and restic encryption passphrase on every single run (save_config explicitly
keeps only non-sensitive values - secrets are re-prompted each run per its
own comment, ~line 70). This matches the README's stated "Manual first"
philosophy but this workspace now has a live OpenBao instance (active
instance at traefik-rs-manager:8200 per this workspace's OpenBao topology
notes) that other services already use for exactly this kind of secret.

By Step 16 (Backup Configuration) Tailscale is already up (installed in
Step 10), so OpenBao would be reachable over the tailnet by the time B2
secrets are needed.

Improvement: add an optional path where bootstrap.sh checks a documented
OpenBao path (e.g. secret/bootstrap/<hostname-or-hardware-uuid>/b2) for the
B2 application key and restic encryption passphrase before falling back to
the interactive prompt, so re-bootstrapping (or bootstrapping a new host
with pre-provisioned secrets) doesn't require a human to type them in from
memory or a credential vault every time. Keep the manual prompt as the
fallback - don't make OpenBao a hard requirement.

File: ex44/bootstrap.sh (secrets prompt section, ~line 200-249 and Step 16
~line 1307).
issue.title: Optionally source B2/restic secrets from OpenBao instead of manual paste every bootstrap run

issue.description:
ADR-1 (docs/plan/plan.md) fixed a corrupted ex44/start.sh and introduced
ex44/sync-start-sh.sh to generate bootstrap.sh's embedded copy from it, but
nothing stops a future edit from being committed without running the sync
script - the exact human-discipline failure that caused the original bug.

Add enforcement: either a git pre-commit hook (this repo has none currently)
that runs `ex44/sync-start-sh.sh --check` (add a --check mode that diffs
without writing and exits nonzero on mismatch) and blocks the commit, or -
since this repo has no Argo Workflow CI wired up yet - at minimum a
documented manual step is not enough; prefer the pre-commit hook since it's
self-contained and doesn't require new CI plumbing.

Files: ex44/sync-start-sh.sh, ex44/bootstrap.sh, ex44/start.sh
issue.notes:
Shipped in 9a03481 (pushed to origin main):

- sync-start-sh.sh: --check mode added (no writes, unified diff on
  mismatch, exit 1; unknown arg = usage error exit 2). Layout-neutral
  messages since the script is self-relative.
- githooks/pre-commit (new, versioned): checks the STAGED pair, not the
  worktree - materializes index start.sh/bootstrap.sh/sync-start-sh.sh
  into a temp dir and runs --check there. Discovers hosts/ex44 then ex44
  from the index, so it keeps working when the restructure lands.
  Activated in this checkout via core.hooksPath=githooks; README
  documents the one-liner for fresh clones (git does not version hooks).
  Replaced the stale untracked .git/hooks/pre-commit left by an earlier
  attempt (worktree-based, hosts/ex44-only).
- Found and fixed live drift: HEAD's embedded copy carried a stray
  '# TEST' debug line (from the IPv6-hardening series) absent from
  start.sh - the exact failure mode this bead targets. bootstrap.sh
  staged as HEAD-minus-that-line so the pair the hook first guards is
  in sync.
- plan.md: ADR-4 records hook-over-CI decision. Tested end to end in a
  scratch repo: drifted commit blocked (diff shown), post-sync commit
  allowed; hook passes on the final index and on the real commit.

Scope note: task description named ex44/ paths, but the worktree holds an
uncommitted ex44/ -> hosts/ex44/ restructure (bead 05901968, from a timed-out
attempt) entangled with two other deferred beads' work (--verify in
bootstrap.sh, SSH-posture README doc). Deliberately NOT committed here -
enforcement landed at HEAD's ex44/ layout with index-only staging so the
pending restructure and its companions stayed untouched in the worktree.
Warning for whoever picks up 05901968: hosts/ex44/start.sh:21 REPO_URL still
points at main/ex44 - committing the move as-is strands self-update on lab
(404 -> bash -n gate makes it no-op harmlessly, but updates never land);
start.sh needs its REPO_URL updated to hosts/ex44 and a version bump so
hosts pull the relocated file via the old URL first. Also .git/hooks has a
new core.hooksPath=githooks local config; the hook tolerates both layouts.

issue.description:
ex44/bootstrap.sh detects IPv6-only hosts (to decide whether to configure
Hetzner's DNS64 for NAT64) with a single check: `ping -4 -c 1 -W 3 1.1.1.1`
(~line 341). If that one ICMP echo is dropped by a transient network blip or
a firewall/provider that blocks ICMP specifically while still permitting
TCP/UDP IPv4 traffic, the host gets misclassified as IPv6-only and configured
with Hetzner's NAT64 DNS servers even though it has perfectly good native
IPv4 - the opposite failure (classifying an actually-IPv6-only host as
dual-stack) is arguably worse but equally possible from one flaky probe.

Improvement: make the connectivity check more robust - e.g. retry a couple
of times before concluding IPv6-only, and/or add a TCP-based fallback check
(e.g. `curl -4 -sf -m 3 https://1.1.1.1` or a raw TCP connect to port 443)
that doesn't depend on ICMP being permitted, only falling back to
IPv6-only/NAT64 config if both signal no IPv4 reachability.

File: ex44/bootstrap.sh ~line 338-346.
issue.title: Harden IPv6-only detection beyond a single ICMP ping
